# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This narrative defines the control, alarm, interlock, and shutdown functions for ammonia screw compressor C-101 and its associated machine room safety systems. It is written for PLC programming and as the basis for Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT). Items marked **[CONFIRM]** are assumptions that need owner or engineer confirmation before coding.

**Control hardware:** Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC. Operator interface is the HMI in the engine room office.

**Equipment covered:**

| Tag | Description |
|---|---|
| C-101 | 400 hp ammonia screw compressor, slide valve capacity control 10-100%, across-the-line soft starter, no VFD |
| PT-101 | Suction pressure transmitter |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure transmitter |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature transmitter |
| II-104 | Motor current transmitter (CT input) |
| AE-110A/B | Machine room ammonia detectors |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan (high speed on alarm) |
| XV-120 | Machine room main liquid solenoid valve |
| BG-1 | Hardwired break-glass emergency stop station, outside machine room |

## 2. Definitions

- **Alarm:** Annunciation only. No equipment action unless stated.
- **Trip:** Compressor stops and a latched fault is set. Restart requires the cause to clear and an operator reset.
- **ESD:** Emergency shutdown of all compressors and de-energizing of XV-120.
- **FLA:** Motor full-load amps (setpoint entered in PLC, **[CONFIRM]** from motor nameplate).

## 3. Operating Modes

C-101 has a Hand/Off/Auto selection, either by HMI or selector **[CONFIRM]**.

- **Off:** Compressor cannot run. Slide valve is unloaded if the compressor is stopped.
- **Hand:** Operator starts and stops the compressor and can raise or lower the slide valve manually. All trips and interlocks remain active. The 95% FLA load limit remains active.
- **Auto:** The PLC starts, stops, and modulates the compressor based on suction pressure.

## 4. Start Permissives

The PLC allows a start only when all of the following are true:

1. No latched trip or ESD is active, and BG-1 is not pressed.
2. Slide valve is at minimum position (unloaded, at or below 10%). If not, the PLC drives it to unload and holds the start until it is.
3. Suction pressure PT-101 is above the low suction trip setpoint (2 psig) and the transmitter signal is healthy.
4. Start counter allows a start (Section 5).
5. Any other package permissives such as oil pump running, oil level, and motor/starter ready **[CONFIRM: vendor package I/O list]**.
6. Ammonia level is below the 150 ppm ESD threshold and no ESD latch is present.

## 5. Start Sequence and Start Limiting

### 5.1 Start sequence

1. A start command (operator in Hand, or Auto demand) is received and permissives are satisfied.
2. The PLC verifies the slide valve is unloaded.
3. The PLC starts the oil pump if the package requires one before compressor start **[CONFIRM]**.
4. The PLC energizes the soft starter run command.
5. A **30-second low oil trip bypass timer** starts at the moment the motor is commanded to run (see Section 7).
6. When the soft starter reports run/bypass confirmed, the compressor is "Running." Failure to confirm within a set time **[CONFIRM, suggest 15 s]** causes a Failed-to-Start fault and trips the compressor.
7. After the compressor is Running and the 30 s bypass has expired, the slide valve is released for loading under capacity control.

### 5.2 Starts-per-hour limit

- Maximum 4 starts in any rolling 60-minute period.
- The PLC logs the timestamp of each start. When 4 starts have occurred in the last 60 minutes, further starts are blocked and the HMI displays "Start Inhibited: Max starts/hour" along with the time remaining until the next start is allowed.
- The limit applies in both Hand and Auto.
- A failed start counts as a start.
- The start count is retained through PLC power cycles **[CONFIRM]**. Resetting it requires supervisor login and is logged.
- A minimum off time between starts **[CONFIRM per soft starter manufacturer]** may also be applied.

## 6. Capacity Control (Auto)

### 6.1 Control basis

Capacity is controlled on suction pressure PT-101 with an adjustable setpoint.

- Default setpoint: **15 psig**
- Adjustable range: **5 to 30 psig**, supervisor login required. The PLC rejects entries outside the range.
- Slide valve range: 10% to 100%

### 6.2 Slide valve actuation

The slide valve is driven by pulsed load and unload outputs.

- When suction pressure is above setpoint plus deadband, the PLC pulses the **load** output. The farther above setpoint, the longer or more frequent the pulses.
- When suction pressure is below setpoint minus deadband, the PLC pulses the **unload** output in the same way.
- Within the deadband, no pulses are issued.
- Pulse width, interval, and deadband are adjustable tuning parameters **[CONFIRM initial values, suggested deadband ±0.5 psi, pulse 0.5-2 s, interval 3-10 s]**.
- The PLC tracks estimated slide valve position, either from a position transmitter or from integrated pulse time **[CONFIRM which]**.
- The PLC does not pulse load past 100% or unload past 10%.

### 6.3 Auto start and stop

- **Auto start:** If the compressor is stopped and suction pressure is above setpoint plus a start differential **[CONFIRM value]** for a start delay time **[CONFIRM]**, the PLC issues a start.
- **Auto stop:** If the compressor is at minimum slide valve position and suction pressure is below setpoint minus a stop differential **[CONFIRM value]** for a stop delay time **[CONFIRM]**, the PLC stops the compressor. The normal stop unloads the slide valve before the motor is stopped.
- Start and stop differentials must be set so that the compressor does not short-cycle. They must also keep the 4 starts per hour limit from being reached under normal operation.
- Auto-stop should not be triggered at suction pressure below the low suction trip.

### 6.4 Motor current limit

The compressor must not load above **95% FLA** as measured by II-104.

- **At or above 95% FLA:** The PLC blocks all load pulses (load inhibit).
- **Above a higher unload threshold** **[CONFIRM, suggest 100% FLA]:** The PLC pulses the unload output until current falls below 95%.
- Load inhibit clears when current falls below **93% FLA** **[CONFIRM hysteresis]**.
- The HMI shows "Load Limited: Motor Current" when active.
- The current limit applies in Auto and Hand.
- During the soft-start acceleration period, the inrush is ignored by the limit logic. The slide valve is held unloaded, so the limit does not act on starting current.
- A sustained overcurrent trip is provided by the starter's own overload protection and is outside this narrative **[CONFIRM]**.

## 7. Protective Alarms and Trips

All trip setpoints are fixed in code or editable by supervisor login only **[CONFIRM]**. Trip conditions are latched. Analog inputs are checked for out-of-range (fault) signals. See Section 7.5.

| Tag | Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDT-102 | Low oil differential alarm | < 35 psid | Alarm |
| PDT-102 | Low oil differential trip | < 25 psid | Trip C-101 |
| TT-103 | High discharge temperature alarm | > 190 °F | Alarm |
| TT-103 | High discharge temperature trip | > 210 °F | Trip C-101 |
| PT-101 | Low suction pressure trip | < 2 psig | Trip C-101 |

### 7.1 Low oil differential pressure (PDT-102)

- Alarm when below 35 psid and trip when below 25 psid.
- **Start bypass:** The low oil trip is bypassed for **30 seconds** after the start command (the motor run output energizing). The bypass timer begins when the motor is commanded to run.
- During the bypass, the low alarm is also suppressed **[CONFIRM]**, though the value is displayed.
- After 30 s, if PDT-102 is below 25 psid, the compressor trips. A trip delay of a few seconds to avoid nuisance trips **[CONFIRM, suggest 3-5 s]** may be applied.
- The bypass applies only at start and does not apply while the compressor is running.
- The bypass timer resets whenever the compressor is stopped.

### 7.2 High discharge temperature (TT-103)

Alarm above 190 °F. Trip above 210 °F. Both have a short confirmation delay **[CONFIRM]**. Alarms auto-clear with hysteresis **[CONFIRM, suggest 3 °F]**.

### 7.3 Low suction pressure (PT-101)

Trip below 2 psig. Because suction pressure may be low normally during startup pull-down, whether this trip is bypassed at start must be decided **[CONFIRM, suggest no bypass, since start is permitted only above 2 psig]**. A short delay of a few seconds is suggested **[CONFIRM]**. A low suction pressure alarm at a value above the trip **[CONFIRM, suggest 4 psig]** is recommended but not specified by the owner.

### 7.4 Trip behavior

On any trip:

1. The PLC removes the motor run command immediately.
2. Slide valve unload output is driven to return the valve to minimum for the next start.
3. The first-out trip cause, timestamp, and process values at trip are logged and shown on the HMI.
4. The trip latches. Restart requires the condition to be cleared and an operator **Reset** at the HMI.
5. A trip does not reset the starts-per-hour count.

### 7.5 Instrument fault handling

If an analog signal (PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104) goes out of range, for example below 3.5 mA on a 4-20 mA loop, the PLC raises an instrument fault alarm. Protection inputs (PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103) failing out of range are treated as a trip condition **[CONFIRM: owner may prefer alarm only]**. Failure of II-104 inhibits loading.

## 8. Machine Room Ammonia Detection and Emergency Response

### 8.1 Detectors

AE-110A and AE-110B are the machine room ammonia detectors. Their signals are used as follows:

- **25 ppm (alarm stage):**
  - Alarm on the HMI and horn/beacon **[CONFIRM]**.
  - Start emergency exhaust fan **EF-201 at high speed**.
  - Compressors continue to run.
- **150 ppm (ESD stage):**
  - Shut down **all compressors** (C-101 and any others).
  - **De-energize XV-120**, the machine room main liquid solenoid (fail-closed valve).
  - EF-201 stays running at high speed.
  - The condition latches.

### 8.2 Voting and fault handling

Voting logic must be defined **[CONFIRM]**. A common arrangement is that either detector (1oo2) at a threshold triggers the action. Detector fault (out-of-range signal) generates an alarm. Whether a detector fault initiates the 25 ppm action is for the owner to decide **[CONFIRM]**.

### 8.3 Reset

- 25 ppm alarm clears automatically when both detectors fall below 20 ppm **[CONFIRM hysteresis]**. EF-201 runs for a minimum run time **[CONFIRM]** after clearing.
- 150 ppm ESD is latched. Reset requires gas concentrations to be below 150 ppm (suggest below 25 ppm) and a manual reset at the HMI **[CONFIRM]**. Resetting the ESD does not automatically restart compressors or reopen XV-120. Reopening XV-120 requires a separate operator action.

### 8.4 Hardwired break-glass emergency stop (BG-1)

- Located outside the machine room.
- Pressing BG-1 causes the same effect as 150 ppm: all compressors stop, XV-120 de-energizes, and EF-201 starts at high speed **[CONFIRM whether EF-201 starts on BG-1]**.
- The ESD function must be **hardwired** so that the compressor run circuit and XV-120 are de-energized independent of PLC operation. BG-1 is also monitored by a PLC input for annunciation and logging.
- BG-1 is wired normally closed (de-energize to trip) so that a wire break causes an ESD.
- Reset requires releasing/resetting the BG-1 station and acknowledging at the HMI.

**Design note:** Consider also hardwiring the 150 ppm detector relay outputs in the ESD chain, so that PLC failure does not defeat that shutdown. The owner should decide this based on the risk assessment and code requirements (IIAR 2, IIAR 9, and local code).

## 9. HMI Requirements

The HMI shall provide:

1. A C-101 overview graphic showing status (Off/Hand/Auto, Running, Tripped), PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, motor %FLA, slide valve position, and setpoint.
2. Suction pressure setpoint entry (supervisor login only, limited to 5-30 psig).
3. Alarm summary with timestamps, acknowledgement, and history.
4. First-out trip indication and reset button.
5. Starts in last hour and time to next allowed start.
6. Machine room ammonia concentration, EF-201 status, XV-120 status, and BG-1 status.
7. User levels: Operator (start, stop, mode, reset, acknowledge) and Supervisor (setpoints, tuning, bypass of start counts). Changes are logged.

## 10. Alarm and Trip Summary

| ID | Description | Type | Latched | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDT-102 L | Oil differential < 35 psid | Alarm | No | Annunciate |
| PDT-102 LL | Oil differential < 25 psid (after 30 s) | Trip | Yes | Stop C-101 |
| TT-103 H | Discharge temp > 190 °F | Alarm | No | Annunciate |
| TT-103 HH | Discharge temp > 210 °F | Trip | Yes | Stop C-101 |
| PT-101 LL | Suction < 2 psig | Trip | Yes | Stop C-101 |
| II-104 | Motor current ≥ 95% FLA | Limit | No | Inhibit load |
| AE-110 H | NH3 ≥ 25 ppm | Alarm | No | EF-201 high speed |
| AE-110 HH | NH3 ≥ 150 ppm | ESD | Yes | Stop all compressors, close XV-120 |
| BG-1 | Break-glass pressed | ESD | Yes | As 150 ppm |
| Start limit | 4 starts in 60 min | Inhibit | No | Block start |
| Failed start | No run confirmation | Trip | Yes | Stop C-101 |

## 11. FAT Test Procedures

Tests are performed with simulated inputs (loop calibrator or PLC force/simulation) and the real HMI. Record pass/fail, tester, and date.

| # | Test | Method | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start permissive, slide valve not unloaded | Set slide position above 10%, command start | Start held; valve unloads; start proceeds when at minimum |
| 2 | Start permissive, trip latched | Latch any trip, command start | Start blocked until reset |
| 3 | Low suction start block | PT-101 < 2 psig, command start | Start blocked |
| 4 | Capacity: load | Auto, PT-101 above setpoint + deadband | Load pulses issued; none within deadband |
| 5 | Capacity: unload | PT-101 below setpoint − deadband | Unload pulses issued |
| 6 | Setpoint range | Enter 4 and 31 psig as supervisor; enter 20 as operator | 4 and 31 rejected; operator entry denied |
| 7 | Setpoint effect | Change setpoint 15 to 20 psig | Control action tracks new setpoint |
| 8 | Slide valve limits | Hold load/unload demand at ends | No pulses beyond 100% and 10% |
| 9 | Current limit | Simulate II-104 at 96% FLA with load demand | Load pulses blocked; HMI message shown |
| 10 | Current limit clear | Lower to below 93% FLA | Loading resumes |
| 11 | Current overshoot | Simulate II-104 above unload threshold | Unload pulses until below 95% |
| 12 | Oil bypass during start | Start with PDT-102 at 10 psid | No trip for 30 s; trip at 30 s (plus delay) |
| 13 | Oil alarm | Running, PDT-102 to 34 psid | Alarm; no trip |
| 14 | Oil trip | Running past 30 s, PDT-102 to 24 psid | Trip; latched; first-out shown |
| 15 | Bypass not re-armed | After trip, reset and restart | Bypass restarts only with new start; not active while running |
| 16 | Discharge temp alarm | TT-103 to 191 °F | Alarm only |
| 17 | Discharge temp trip | TT-103 to 211 °F | Trip |
| 18 | Low suction trip | Running, PT-101 to 1.9 psig | Trip |
| 19 | Trip reset | Clear condition, reset | Trip clears only after reset and with condition clear |
| 20 | Starts per hour | Perform 4 starts in under 60 min, attempt fifth | Fifth start blocked; countdown shown; allowed when oldest start is 60 min old |
| 21 | Gas 25 ppm | Either detector to 25 ppm | Alarm; EF-201 high speed; compressors keep running |
| 22 | Gas 150 ppm | Either detector to 150 ppm | All compressors stop; XV-120 de-energizes; latched |
| 23 | Gas reset | Lower gas, reset | Reset only with manual action; no auto restart; XV-120 stays closed until operator action |
| 24 | Break-glass | Press BG-1 with PLC in program mode or powered off if feasible | Compressor run circuit and XV-120 de-energize regardless of PLC |
| 25 | BG-1 wire break | Open BG-1 circuit | ESD |
| 26 | Instrument fault | Open PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 loops one at a time | Instrument fault alarm and defined action (Section 7.5) |
| 27 | Detector fault | Open AE-110A, then AE-110B loop | Fault alarm; action per owner decision |
| 28 | Mode check | Test Hand/Off/Auto | Trips active in all modes; Off cannot run |
| 29 | Failed start | Block run confirmation | Failed-start trip after timeout |
| 30 | Power cycle | Cycle PLC power during run and trip | Defined restart behavior; trips remain latched **[CONFIRM]**; no auto restart |

## 12. Open Items for Owner/Engineer

1. Motor FLA and starter overload arrangement.
2. Detector voting logic and detector fault action.
3. Whether the 150 ppm ESD and BG-1 are hardwired into the starter and XV-120 circuits (strongly recommended) and EF-201 behavior on BG-1.
4. Low suction pressure trip bypass and delay, and the response to instrument faults on protective inputs.
5. Auto start/stop differentials and delays, and capacity control tuning values.
6. Oil pump and other package permissives, per the compressor vendor.
7. Slide valve position feedback or time-based estimate.
8. Start counter retention and reset policy; minimum off time per soft starter.
9. Applicable code requirements (IIAR 2, IIAR 9, NFPA 70, local) for ventilation and detection setpoints and ESD.
